Pathway to Happiness
   pathwaytohappiness.com/courses/self-mastery-course-1/05-perspective
                                                                          May 7, 2019



05 Perspective

We’re moving all courses to the new Self Mastery Community

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/28N0fpNcTgM

Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Perspective lesson audio

2. Write about your thoughts, emotions, and behavior from a third person
perspective.
You can write on your computer or written journal. You might also write on your phone.
It is okay to experiment and find a method so you can write consistently.

3. At some point your mind will shift into an observer perspective about your
thoughts and emotions. This might happen as soon as you write, or it might take a
couple weeks for that shift to take place.

Some notes
This is building on The Attention exercise in session 3. Instead of just “noticing” you are
doing something conscious to shift perspective. Also, by writing about yourself, you are
focusing your attention inward. Focusing your attention inward in a neutral observer
perspective is different than focusing inward in a judgmental, fearful, or victim manner.

Whether you notice a shift into the observer perspective right away or not is not critical.
If you don’t feel it happening, that is fine. Don’t worry about it. OR, better yet, write
about the voices in your head are worried about it.

There are benefits even if you don’t see the shift happening. The practice here is
helping you prepare for session 7 and 10. Together these practices are designed to
move you further into the neutral observer perspective even further. Third person
writing can have benefits on its own, but also prepares you for later practices.

You are breaking the hypnotic effects of the identity you have built up in your mind.

                                                                                                                                           1/5

This is largely anchored in language. The terms “I” and “me” are signals to the brain to
insert self images created in the past. When it does this it fixates your perspective,
which then rolls into habitual uses of your attention. By shifting your sense of identity
you are shifting your perspective in a practical and powerful way.

Some of this may bring up uncomfortable feelings, and realizations. That’s okay. You
will get a practice for working with those feelings in the next session on Acceptance.

Resistance to change
 It is likely that certain parts of your mind will feel uncomfortable with this exercise. Parts
will protest, procrastinate, and feel uncomfortable with this shift. This is very
understandable as this practice is counter-intuitive to the ways you have thought of, and
sensed your identity.

One of the best practices is to apply this third person writing to the resistance. Write
about the feelings, and the thoughts that are part of this resistance. These are the very
parts of your mind that you want to step outside of, and see from a different
perspective. If you have these resistance parts of your mind, be sure to write about
them. It will reveal to you things helpful for you to see.

There may be part of your mind looking for a certain outcome or change. Write about
this part of your mind fixated on this expectation. You may find it odd, that your mind
could have a notion about what is “supposed to happen” even though you have never
done this practice or have no knowledge of it. This kind of an “all knowing” part is living
in a false belief. It is even living in a false belief about “when” it is supposed to occur.

Identifying these false belief and false thought generating aspects of your mind is the
kind of “small stuff” that will be helpful as you progress to dismantling bigger beliefs and
emotional reactions.

One of the reasons there is resistance to this specific exercise is that you are going
against the mind’s decades of building an identity image of your “self”. This identity
image, is your mind’s version of who you are. In this third person writing exercise the
intent is for you to shift into a consciousness as your identity.

This shift into a different sense of your identity upsets the “normal” and habitual routines
of neural pathways the brain has been using when it uses words like “I” and “me.” You
are throwing a wrench into the machinery of your brain. Or, more literally, you are
waking up your consciousness in the middle of an automated stream of neural
pathways firing and creating new neural pathways. Or, you might just say that you are
going up against the ego.

It was probably the type of change you were looking for and so this is what you asked
for. It just doesn’t look like what your old mind expected it to look like.



                                                                                                                                    2/5

Common questions

If I am not "I" or "me" then what am I?
You have always been “you”, however you are now becoming aware of how your mind
can create mental versions of you. As you see that, your mind reacts with surprise that
it’s “mental constructs of you” aren’t the real you. So it gives you this question.

You can even step outside the part of the mind asking this question and see that it isn’t
“you” either. As you shift out of these different mental versions you move into
awareness of your Self as consciousness. From a consciousness perspective you can
see how the mind creates multiple false versions of “I” and “me” and stories about who
you are.

Watch the two Youtube videos below on Self Image and do the exercise. Practice
stepping into the observer and conscious awareness and see how quickly the mind can
create new versions.

Pay particular attention to the “YOU” that is creating the different versions.

Am I conscousness?
That’s what I have been trying to tell you. Or at least point you towards. Maybe there is
another term for it, and maybe as you progress you will discover you are something
else on the other side of consciousness. Either way, you first have to move out of the
mind’s mental image, memory, beliefs, and projected images of what you are and into
consciousness. From there it is a mystery of how to define the “Self.” From this state of
consciousness you can move into false identities of the mind. The Judge and Victim are
just two of these false characters that you as consciousness can occupy.

However, some things we know for sure, “You are.” You exist. You perceive, and You
Express.

What should I write about?
Start by writing about what is going on today and this past week. This is usually an
easier starting point.

If your mind still can’t pick something then sit down and write down the thoughts going
through your head as you look at the paper or screen. Write about what is going on in
your head RIGHT NOW.

If you regularly do this, you will be practicing becoming the observer of your mind in
real time. It is this awareness skill that will allow you to make changes in the NOW of
real them.

What if I have too much to write about?
Then write about the part of your mind telling you the story that “IT has too much to
write about”.

                                                                                                                                    3/5

See what I did there? I just did the writing assignment. I wrote about that part of your
mind as if it wasn’t you, and that’s a step in the right direction. Write about the parts of
the mind telling you that you have too much or too little or that you don’t know what to
write about. They are all just parts of the mind that you have hypnotized your self to
believe.

Should I write about significant events in my past?
First write about the part of your mind that is struggling with the question of what to
write about.

Example: “There is a voice in Gary’s head really wondering if Gary should write about
what happened when he was 10 years old. That voices feels it is really important that
that issue be resolved, but there wasn’t specific instructions about a specific time frame,
he is concerned he will get it wrong. Part of Gary really wants to let go of that emotion
from that memory, but another part seems to disagree and think Gary isn’t ready for
that yet.”

This is what I mean by writing about what is going on NOW, or at least today and this
week.

Later you can write about more significant things of the past. It will be more beneficial
once you have better established your observer perspective.

What is the most important thing to write about?
Write about events or thoughts that have emotion to them. However, at this point the
exercise is for you to build up the strength of your Observer Consciousness and be able
to maintain it. You will slip in and out during the day depending on the amount of
emotion. So what you write about is not so important as that you exercise the muscle of
being in that Observer Consciousness during the day. Events or thoughts with too
strong of emotions may pull you out of observer mode.

At this point you get the benefit of developing the Observer Consciousness no matter
what you write about. But you only get that benefit through writing, so just write. Later
the writing will be more focused.

How much time should I spend writing?
That depends. If you have more time,then spend it writing. If you are a single mom of 2
kids and and have a full time job, then you will likely have less time. I hesitate to put a
number of minutes during the day because different people have different resources of
time, energy, attention, and motivation. If I put a number that might be right for you,
then it won’t be the right amount of time for the next person.

With that said, if you can, write for at least 20 minutes a day for most days. If you can do
more some days, great, if it is only 5 minutes some days, then that is still a benefit.

Who is the real "I"?


                                                                                                                                    4/5

That’s what you are on your way to finding out? You don’t get that answer by having it
handed to you via text on a website. You remove yourself from the false “I” and “me”
versions of the ego mind, and the real you will remain.

This seems weird. Is there any reason this would benefit me?
Yes. There are now studies as to how referring to yourself in third person improves your
ability to set expectations, regulate emotions, and cooperate with others.

Read the article

Supporting videos

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/qlt07d89c8E

How you see your “self”.

There is a mechanism in the mind that allows it to project an image or an idea of what
you are and then for you to feel like that is you. This is very powerful, but doesn’t give
you an accurate representation of what you are.

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/0mhSnXIWYL0

Who are you really?

When I have people do this exercise there are two important aspects to notice. First is
to see how the mind not only makes multiple false images of you, but how each one
can seem real when you are in that point of view. The other aspect to notice is how you
as consciousness can make your mind do this at will.

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/-o-kWkUmZn0

Resistance to doing the writing in third person?

You aren’t the only one. A lot of people run into that in the beginning. One of the keys,
start small. Maybe one sentence to begin with. Or just commit to writing for 5 minutes.
That’s a success.
Also, it’s okay if it is chaotic and jumps around. Your mind is probably jumping around
with thoughts so that’s fine to put it on the page that way.





                                                                                                                                     5/5

Fundamental to this session on Perspective is that it’s an exploration of the imagination
and the power of the imagination in both creating emotions and false images of
ourselves, and if we are to find the truth of who are, we need to distance ourselves from
those illusions. So enjoy and good luck.

If we look at what makes up a belief we will see several different elements. There is
perspective, (also referred to as Point of View) the thought or idea, emotion, and faith.
Sometimes, particularly in the case of big or emotionally strong beliefs, it is difficult to
change all these elements at once. Fortunately, you don’t have to. In this exercise you’ll
learn to practice changing your perspective. In this way you will learn to change beliefs
in a step by step manner. Changing perspective is the easiest place element to change
when you start, and once you change perspective, the other elements change much
more easily.

This first exercise I want to take you through a little meditation that will help change
your point of view, so that perhaps when I discuss it, it will give a different perspective
than what we traditionally would have taken. For this exercise we will need to be sitting
comfortably, quietly or laying down, as few distractions of noise as possible, and I want
you to close your eyes, put your attention on your breath and let your body relax. Let
your whole body to just melt and sink into wherever you’re sitting or lying down, and
take a couple of deep breaths, and let yourself exhale, letting everything go. And just let
that body be perfectly still. There’s no need to move it yet at this time. Just notice what
it’s doing. I want you to let everything in your mind go blank, let everything dissolve.
We’ll go on a journey of perception and a tour of the imagination, and we’ll have fun on
this travel and maybe take a look at things in a way we haven’t before. And so for that let
everything go, until there’s just you and your breath. It’s just you, observing that body
and what that breath is doing to that body. Nothing for you to do, just observe. And just
for fun I want you to imagine that you’re having a dream. You’re having a dream and in
that dream you’re just starting to become aware that you’re inhabiting this body. In this
dream you’re inhabiting this body and you’re just watching this body breathe in and
out. And you know that you’re dreaming, because you’re very acutely aware that your
real body, the one you used to inhabit, is back at home, in your bad, sleeping. Imagine
that you are having a lucid dream, and in that dream you’re just waking up to become
aware that you’re dreaming. And that this dreaming body that you’re in is breathing, it’s
sitting or it’s lying down, and you can begin to notice it’s posture, what it’s body is
feeling, the effects of gravity on the feet, on the back, wherever you’re touching the floor,
wherever you’re seated, the pressure that’s on that body, and you’re just noticing how

                                                                                                                           1/12

that physical body is experiencing this dream. I also want you to notice that this body
can hear. The body you’re inhabiting has ears and you can notice the sounds that that
body can hear.

Notice here that I’m careful to give you a language that there’s you, and you’re separate
from that body, although at present you’re inhabiting that body. And I heighten this by
describing that your normal body is some place else sleeping, to let yourself imagine
you’re something quite different than just physical body. You’re a consciousness, you
are the Observer, you don’t even know what you are as you’re having this dream, but
you know you’re here, inhabiting the body that you’re experiencing, and that you can
perceive and be aware of all that the senses of that body can perceive. And notice how
that body hears sounds, how it breathes, notice that you don’t have to do a thing for that
body – it knows just what to do all by itself. It’s breathing, it’s pumping blood, it’s
bringing nutrients to all the cells, it’s eliminating all the toxins – every cell knows
exactly what to do. And it’s not you that’s guiding all that. It has its own intelligence. I
want you to notice that you can perceive whatever that body is feeling. You can also
perceive the emotions that it’s feeling. And the emotions that it’s feeling aren’t really
yours, they just belong to that body – it’s the emotional experience that that body is
having.

Now, make it a little more interesting. I want you to notice just one finger. Don’t move
your finger yet. I want you to notice that you can direct the actions and movements of
that body, and we’re going to start with just one finger, but I want you to put your
attention on one finger, and notice how you, consciousness, have the ability to move
one finger. Just have a sense of it, sense that there’s you and that you have the ability to
intend and activate the movement of the finger. I want you (1) to be aware of yourself as
the observer and director of this, (2) be aware of the kind of message that you send to
that finger in order for it to move. (3) The third element is the response, which is the
movement of that finger. That finger is going to respond to your message. (4) And the
fourth element is what is the sensation that that body is experiencing while moving. So
with great awareness to these elements, go ahead and move a finger, move it back and

up and down, notice third how that finger responds to your message, and fourth notice
the sensation that has changed by movement: maybe it’s pressing harder against

weight that it’s holding on, it’s working harder, the muscles are engaged. Notice that
there’s feedback to tell you and confirm that something has happened, that your
message has been sent and delivered.

Now that you understand the elements, we’ll go for something a little bigger. And I want
you to put your attention on one of your arms and on all four of those elements: you, the
message you send to move an arm, how all the muscles engage and the action of that

Notice how you direct it’s movement. Notice the sensation that comes back. Is it
pressing against something? Is it rushing through the air and you can feel a coolness on

                                                                                                                           2/12

one side and nothing on the other? What are the feelings that you get back, the
sensations that you get back to tell you it’s actually moving and that your message has
been delivered and action is being taken by those muscles? Notice how those sensations
confirm your experience that the arm is moving. This will become very important later.
It tells us that what we said would happen is happening. And go ahead and let your arm

The next thing I want you to do is again stay still and this time imagine raising your

again? Are you reliving the experience emotionally as well? Let us say that we are, at

least to some degree, getting all the emotional and physical sensory feedback as if this
virtual reality of our imagination is actually happening again, we’re replaying the
emotion, as well as the sensory feeling in our body.

And at this point I’d like you to again let that whole dream go, recognizing that it was
just a dream that you created in the imaginary world, just the way you imagined you
raised your arm. Let those dreams dissolve and put your attention on that breath, and
notice again that you are the Observer and that you can direct that physical body’s
actions and you can observe what it senses, and notice also that you have directed the
virtual world of the imagination: you’ve called up a memory, you’ve gone inside it,
you’ve gotten to experience it with all its sensory feedback and you’ve just exited it, and
dissolved it along with all the emotions and sensory feedback that it was creating in
your system. Then put your attention on your breath and just notice the sensory
feedback from being present here in the body that you’re in. By now your emotional
state has probably shifted from what you were experiencing in the memory, and your
breath is quite a pleasant experience.

It’s wonderful what you can do with your attention. It’s wonderful what you can do
when you direct it and focus it in regards to how you can shift your own dream and how
you feel emotionally. That concludes our little dream ride in the imagination, and
welcome back to this dreaming experience and don’t be so sure that your body is not
actually some place else, sleeping, but maybe one day you wake up and remember this
dream. You’re welcome to open your eyes now, and move about and listen to the rest of
the program however you like.

One of the biggest challenges talked about in personal development and growth is
always about erasing your personal history. This is another way of saying the ego’s
identity. There’re many ways to go dissolve your personal history or ego. I am going to
share with you the one that I use most effectively in small steps and sometimes in huge
leaps with my clients. That exercise is to write about your self. I’ve written many times
about parts of my life. And, at different times, I’ve rewritten the same story about the
same event, multiple times. Of course, each time I write it comes out different, but
that’s because I am not the same person I was when I wrote it last time. As a matter of
fact after a year of intense work,,,  it was quite astonishing how much my story changed.
And that was largely because I was writing it from a completely different point of view.
The person I believed I was a year before wasn’t the person I was a year later.

Part of the whole problem with writing about ourselves are the pronouns “I”, and “me”.
These words are very limiting words. For starters they don’t give any indication that we
are different now than we were in the past. When we go and tell something that
happened to us in our past, we always talk about “I”. Even if it was something that
happened 10 years ago or 30 years ago, we say “I was there and I did this and I did
that.” We also say “This happened to me,” “he did this to me,” “she did this to me.”
Well, in that story, that “me”, that we are imagining as “me”, was the “me” that we were
10, 20, 30 yeas ago. It is not the ME of today. Yet if we look at it with common sense,
there’s no way we’re the person we were 10 or 20, or 30 years ago. We are now very
                                                                                                                           4/12

much a different person living a different life. We’ve had other experiences, but we talk
about “I” and “me” in the past, as if we are the same person we are today that we were
then. Largely the problem is that when we go back in our memory of back then, let’s just
say 10 years ago, we imagine the story in our imagination, in our virtual reality, and
right there that story plays, and we put ourselves in that imagined experience as if it’s
happening again. Literally we bring into our imagination the past, just like we did in
that exercise. And we experience the past today. And in that regard it does feel like no
time has elapsed. And it feels again like “I” am there and things are happening to “me”
again. That’s how we can remember things like they happened yesterday. Because our
imagination creates a virtual reality simulation with all the pictures, the sounds and the
sensory feedback as if it were really happening again. That’s why memory is so
powerful. Because we create it again and again and again in our virtual reality of the
imagination. Well this can be a wonderful thing, cause it allows us to go into the world
of the imagination and create incredible worlds and experience all the feedback, as if it’s
happening again. But it also can be not such a wonderful thing, because we can go back
to memory and replay stories that were terrible experiences in our lives, or unhappy
experiences. And we can play that unpleasant experience over and over, and over, and
over again. And it feels like we’re still there. This is not such a good thing. And what we
actually do is we indulge repeatedly in that same unpleasant emotion, and it can
actually stir it up and make it thicker and thicker, and thicker, and make ourselves more
upset or more depressed.

This can also happen if someone tells us what happened, or if we have to go talk to
someone about what happened, and we tell the story over and over again, and we re-live
in the virtual reality of what happened last week or yesterday, and we tell it over and
over again to all our friends, each time indulging in the emotion. You could say each
time we are giving more and more life to that memory, or you could also say we’re
amplifying and making more solid our personal history. Now, it’s no longer happening
to us. It happened yesterday and it happened 2 days ago and 3 days ago, and every day
that goes by it goes further and further back, but if we tell the story, we can make it
more and more virtually real, real in our virtual reality anyways.

Sometimes we say it’s good to tell the story to get it out. Well, it’s good to get our
emotions out, but it’s not good emotionally to indulge in it and exacerbate any
unpleasant feelings by reliving a virtual reality that no longer exists, and imagining
ourselves as if we were then, when it’s no longer us. You see, we play that story “I” and
“me” in that virtual reality story, whether we’re imagining it or we’re telling that to a
friend, and we’re reliving it as if that’s happening again. Well, that’s no longer “us”. The
imagined, or virtual “us” is not us. But we get tricked into that false identity perspective
by the words “I” and “me.”

That past experience now only exists in the virtual reality of our imagination and
memory. And even if we go there, it’s no longer happening to us, because our physical
human is the one that’s sitting here in this room, imagining going through it again. You
see how there’re two dreams here: 1) there’s the one you’re sitting in the room, or

                                                                                                                           5/12

wherever you are right now and then 2) there’s the one that’s the virtual reality of your
imagination, where you go experience something from your past, as if it were real.
There is the real self and there is the virtual simulation of self generated by our
imagination.  Just like imagining raising your arm might have seemed real and had
some sensory feedback physically was a virtual self. Or the memory I had you visit had
emotion as if it were real even though you were in the perspective of the virtual self
from your past when you created it.

If you can clarify which one is which, that you are never and you will never be the
person that you were in the past, you can play the tape in your memory, but it’s no
longer you. You’re not the person you used to be and you never will be. Whatever
happened to you in the past, isn’t what’s happening to you now. You can create the
imaginary story that feels it’s happening again, but that is clearly what you’re creating in
your virtual reality. And as you’ve just found out: you are the one that can sit and direct
the virtual reality show or you can change it, you can turn a memory on and you can
turn it off, you can walk into it or you can step outside of it. The same way you send
your messages to your body to make it move, you can send the messages to that
imagination and alter that story, and alter the point of view you see it from

Why I want this to be so clear is because you’re going to write the stories of what’s in
your memory. You’re going to write the experiences of your past. But you’re not going to
write them from the point of view of “I” or “me” as first person, because you’re the
person sitting in the room today, in this moment. You aren’t even the person you were
yesterday. You’ve changed in the last 24 hours. You’ve changed in the last 30 minutes.
So I want you to write that story of events in the past but with the awareness that you
are writing about the Virtual self. You are going to write a kind of autobiography, but
you’re going to write it more as a biography, because you’re going to write it in third
person. You’re going to refer to yourself as “he” or “she”, “him” or “her”, or by name, or
if the first name is a little awkward you can remove yourself a little bit and write about
yourself using your middle name.

When you write this biography, I want you to write about two different portions of these
interactions: 1) The first part is the external part. What you said and what this other
person said, and what they did and what you did (of course you’re going to write about
it in third person, where you refer to yourself as “he” or “she”). So, you write about the
external actions. 2) But also, and this part is more important, you are going to write
about what went on in your mind: what were you saying to yourself, what emotions did
you have, what did you agree to, what did you commit to, what did you defend in your
mind, what were all the thoughts that you had. You’ll write it out as “She thought to
herself”, “This really pissed her off”, “She got more and more angry”, and “She
committed to never talking to this person again”, “When she was driving home from
that interaction, she played in her imagination the scene again and again, and again,
that made her more and more upset”. This is how you write the story. Using “she”: what
her thoughts were, what her emotions were, what she agreed to or he agreed to in her
mind. Write out the words that went through HER mind. Write out the images that

                                                                                                                           6/12

went through HIS head. In this practice you are becoming aware that there is a virtual
self running around in your imagination. You see, we’ve got to disassociate from
believing that the “I” and “me” of the story in our head is the “I” who we are now.

The structure of the writing is very much what works for you. In terms of what time
frame you’re going to write about. My suggestion is that you start small and you journal
all the events of the day or the past week, that you get used to writing of yourself, even
in this current week, of what happened yesterday and the day before in third person.
What happened this morning is no longer you. The critical events to write about are the
ones where you had emotional reactions, whether they are great, high, ecstatic, happy
emotional reactions or those that take you down into unpleasant experiences. Write
about both of those types. If there wasn’t any emotional reaction, then there probably
isn’t as much content for good agreement finding in there. That’s fine. You can still
write about things that had very little to no emotion as well.

At this stage it’s not important to find any specific beliefs or change them. The
important part of this exercise is to shift your perspective and separate your self from
this virtual self that does all the simulations and gets caught in the stories in your head.
 This separation is important because it is necessary in order to change all the beliefs we
will find later.

Why I have you start with recent events is because most of those are pretty minor
emotional reactions. One of the challenges we get into, when we do this assignment, if
we start writing about very intense emotional experiences, what often happens is we
start reliving that memory as if we are there again, and this is a big trap we do not want
to fall into. If you find yourself writing about an experience or going back to a memory
that has a lot of emotional content, and you feel yourself as if you’re there again, and it’s
happening all over, we have lost that clarity and awareness, and now we’re inside our
virtual reality, experiencing it as it were real. When we get caught into the perspective of
first person in one of our stories, this just makes us believe all those stories and
reactions again. The result is that we end up reinforcing in the mind the perspective of
the virtual self memory and the reactions. If this happens, if you find yourself in the first
person perspective of a story, I want you to close your book, stop writing in your journal
and go do something fun and playful. Exercise or take a nap. If you were typing it into
your computer, turn it off and take a break.

To avoid getting caught up in the perspective of a past virtual self, I want you to start
with smaller experiences, less emotional charge, so you can practice being aware of
watching the memory of an experience you had back then, while being outside of it.
You’re watching the holographic virtual reality of imagination, and you can see yourself
in that dream, and yet you remain the observer of the outside, writing about what
happened in that memory. You are writing in third person, but you’re learning to look at
yourself in those memories as if it really is, or was another person. Writing from third
person helps you to do this, it automatically makes you shift your point of view, so
you’re looking at the memory of yourself from outside. This is how we’re going to be
able to redirect our imagination. If we get inside the memory, that memory takes us
                                                                                                                           7/12

along for a ride, and we end up for the emotional ride, wherever that goes. It’s harder to
control. But if we’re on the outside, watching our virtual selves on the inside of that
memory, we can turn it off, we can rewrite it, we can look for other choices, and other
interpretations with a much greater sense of awareness, a much more expanded point of
view.

What will be happening while you do this exercise is you could say there is a sense that
your attention is split: 1) there’s the part of us that is outside, The Observer, watching
that virtual character that we used to be have that experience; 2) and we are also partly
in the point of view of that character having that experience. As long as we can remain
50% or more on the outside and be aware of what that character on the inside was
experiencing, we can keep writing, but when we feel emotions overwhelm you, then it’s
time to close the book and to go have a break from the process. If this happens with an
event we are writing about from far in your past, then perhaps wait on writing about
that event until you have practiced some of the other exercises as well.

So, start with smaller events, things that have happened this week and this month. So
much of this exercise is about learning to manage your imagination, instead of having
that imagination take you for a ride, and lose track that it’s not real. But in the sensory
experience feedback we get it seems so real. So we’re gathering awareness about how
that imagination works, how the emotional feedback from the imagination works and
learning to realize that what we’re experiencing, even though we have the emotion,
doesn’t have anything to do with what’s going on today in this reality.

What you may find is when you write about something and it has an emotional charge
to it, you can have that emotional charge while you’re writing it. And if you can stay in
the “witness-observer” mode, watching yourself in that dream, writing about it in third
person, keep writing. Having emotions from the memory or virtual story come out is
fine, as long as it doesn’t complete absorb us into the perspective of that first person
virtual character.

One of the things you may find out is that after you finished writing you’re still at
emotional charge to it. What I’ve recommended clients do and what I recommend you
to do is that if there’s still an emotional charge, go back a day or two later and read
what you wrote. This helps change your perspective even more. You’ll be reading what
a past virtual self from two days ago wrote about a second past virtual self from 4 days
ago. Perhaps even read through that story slowly being aware of the separation between
you, The Observer, and the two other virtual characters. You might come back every
few days and re-read these writings. Coming back after a couple days, you will be in a
different perspective and the things you thought, said, and believed in the first version,
typically won’t be as believable when you revisit them in following days.

Then, if there is still emotion, and you can stay more than 50% in the outside observer
perspective, write about the original event again. Don’t rewrite the same story, but go
back to that memory, observe it from the outside and rewrite it. The second rewrite will
have a different point of view about that experience. You will find that by going and
                                                                                                                           8/12

writing your story, by watching it from the outside and writing about it, you’re putting
your attention on that story and by putting your attention on that story and on that
emotion, it is being modified, your whole point of view and awareness, and your
consciousness are all shifting. This is huge. After you’ve written it the second time and
there may still be more emotion there, go back and read the whole thing over following
days. You’ll find out that each time you retell it from the outside, it helps dissipate the
emotion. This is very different than if we tell the story from the inside, as if it’s
happening again with the terms “I” and “me”. Which is usually what happens when we
tell our friends and family, or rally people to “our” side, and reinforce all the emotions
of the “virtual self.” Usually when we tell the story from that point of view, the emotions
amplify. But when we tell the story from the outside, third person, each time you’re
writing, each time you’re reading, the emotions dissipate. That’s because by observing
the story and putting our attention on it from the outside, we’re modifying the story.
Even if the only thing we are consciously modifying at this stage is the perspective of the
story, it still has an impact of changing other aspects of the story.

So, you’re going to rewrite the historical parts of your life. And you’re going to write it as
if it was lived by someone else. Cause in fact it was. It wasn’t lived by the person you are
today. The person who you were back then in those moments – that’s who lived your
life, and you’re not that person anymore. And all the agreements you made about
yourself back then were made about the person who you were then, and they do not
apply to who you are now. You might have carried a lot of them forward, so all those
virtual beliefs feel like real things, but that part is changeable.

And the first part to change is Point of View.

I was working with a client, and she was challenged with some relationship issues. It
had to do with men, and she deduced from our conversation and my questioning that it
had to do with her father. The relationship dynamic that she’d started living with him
when she was a young girl had carried forward to her adult relationships with men. She
said: “I think I understand, let me share with you what happened when I was a little
girl.” I told her “No. She’s like “But I want to tell you the story, I want to tell you what
happened, I think I understand now why I do what I do,” and I told her “No.” It was
very peculiar, she was very surprised cause I’m usually very open and receptive to what
people want to share, and she was kind of adamant, and I was more adamant and I said
“No,” and then she said “Why not?”, I said “You’re welcome to tell me the story, but this
is how I want you to tell me the story: I want you to go write it down, and I want you to
write it down in third person.” And I gave her the assignment I gave you. She thought it
kind of odd, and I didn’t explain to her why, but I knew right then that if she told me the
story again about what happened in her past, from the same point of view she lived 30
years ago, which was a victim point of view, which was a judgment point of view, which
was an abandonment point of view, then she was going to be experiencing that history
again, reliving her virtual self then, as if it were happening, and reinforcing her mind to
dream from that point of view, of victim, of abandonment, of judgment. That’s why I
didn’t let her tell her story. What was more important was that she look at the story

                                                                                                                           9/12

from the outside. Only be being on the outside can we pull it apart. She did the writing
and, she did find all the false agreements she made that she agreed to way back then
when she was a little girl. That was just misinterpretation, because she didn’t
understand what was going on.

So, start with this week, continue on with this month and each day, or several times a
week, whatever your schedule allows, start writing different experiences of your life.
Write the biography – that biography that somebody else, who you used to be, lived.
And be clear to stay outside of that virtual reality, watching the memory, not getting
hooked into the point of view of that memory, not reliving it, noticing it’s there, it has a
life, it has emotions, and as we observe the life of that memory, as we sit outside and
watch it, and we put our attention on, just by the fact of writing it our attention is on it,
and we tell the story of that person and what happened to them then, and what they did
and what they believed, then we are more and more aware, that we are watching a
virtual reality. And don’t get caught.

One of the hugest items about this exercise, is that I’m giving here the element of how
we change the belief. No one ever tells us how to change a belief. A lot of times we
decide: “Ok, we’re going to commit to something else.” We discover we believe we are
ugly, so we decide to commit: “Ok, I’m going to believe I’m beautiful.” But nowhere did
we ever dissolve the belief that we are ugly. You see, that belief doesn’t actually get
changed by believing something else. No, we just build something on top of it. But the
belief that we are ugly is still there. This is why it is very important to change your
personal history, to completely dissolve it. This means going and dissolving all the
agreements you have about yourself. We find them in our stories, in our memory. And
the way to modify them is to become aware of them, and put our attention on them,
knowing that they are not true, that they are just part of the virtual illusion in our
imagination – something called a “virtual reality”, that we make a mistake of thinking
that it’s real.

So, enjoy the writing, and maybe, just as an exercise, after you write some of these
stories, and you take the emotional charge out of them and find out that you can change
how you write the story, you can look at an old experience in a completely different way.
So, to stretch yourself at this point, after rewriting it, and after the emotion is out of it or
mostly out of it, you can rewrite it from another person’s point of view (that one who
you talked to or interacted with). So, write the story from his point of view and see how
it shifts entirely again. That will help you completely invalidate your side and go faster
in erasing your history. And some times, just for fun, write the story again as a comedy.
To make fun of yourself and other people. So that you don’t take yourself so seriously.
This is another way to change your personal history, change your whole point of view
about who you used to be, and by letting go of who you used to be, you will be more and
more who you really are, which is the one directing the whole show.

For some people there can be a lot of resistance to writing. There might be all sorts of
distracting and procrastinating questions like: I don’t know what to write about.
Should I use a computer and type, or a journal and write. Should I write in cursive, or
                                                                                                                       10/12

print? Should I use a pen or a pencil? All sorts of questions, fears, and doubts can
come up to distract us. If this happens and you have difficulty getting started, then
what I want you to do is write about the resistance you feel. Write third person about
what is going on right then with your fears, doubts, and distracting questions. It might
be something like. “Sarah sat staring at the blank journal. A part of her wanted
desperately for there to be immediate results. However another part of her mind
chimed in with the thought, “There is no way this is going to help. It might help other
people but you are different. This won’t work for you.” This voice seemed so confident.
 It was odd how confident this voice could sound while other parts of her were so
skeptical and unsure about things. It seemed like this voice in Sarah’s head was telling
her not to do the assignment. The voice was telling her in a confident tone that the
process would be a failure. Another part of Sarah’s seemed to agree, and felt like there
was no point. It was a virtual version of Sarah that felt defeated before even starting.
As Sarah began watching these two parts of her mind, she began to wonder how they
could claim to know so much. Did they know what was in the Self Mastery Course? Did
they know what assignments would be next and how they would build on each other?
Of course not. Sarah began to see that these voices in her head only seemed to know
about a virtual or imagined future and her virtual self of the past.”

Sometimes people just have a plain resistance to writing, even resistance to writing
about their resistance. Sometimes the issue is just more practical because it takes time,
and they don’t have much. If life is busy and sitting down to write doesn’t fit into your
schedule very well, then there is another thing you can do. Get a little office memo
recorder. They sell them at office supply stores for voice recording. Something that can
record a couple hours would be plenty. Make voice notes instead of written notes. Make
these notes about your thoughts, emotions, behaviors, etc in the same third person
references described earlier. Just as if you were writing them third person. Then listen
to these recordings the next day, or a couple days later. As you listen to these thoughts
that were recorded, you will be the outside observer of your thoughts. This is the
outside observer practice that we are looking for in this assignment. Yes it will probably
be weird talking about your virtual self in third person. But what is more weird is to do
nothing about them.

Perhaps keep it in your car and make voice notes to your self when you are alone.
Maybe you have an office by your self and you can close the door. Then play them
back later that day, even an hour or a few minutes later is enough for you to become an
observer of those thoughts depending on the situation and how charged up you are
emotionally. With practice you will get to a point of view that you will feel outside these
thoughts as they are happening, but you will have to practice to get there. After some
time, you will notice that your mind is just thinking, stories, and ramblings, often
jumping around to different topics all by itself. It isn’t really you doing the thinking.
 It’s a virtual world in the imagination with a virtual self being taken for the ride. This
might be a little strange at this point, but this is progress. This is you detaching from




                                                                                                                           11/12

your thoughts and beliefs. You are taking the first steps, you are detaching from the
Point of View part of your thoughts and beliefs. After practicing this part, detaching
from the rest of it, including the emotions will be much easier and faster.

Measuring Progress and Managing Expectations

Something to note at this point. We are not looking to make some kind of struck by
lightning “oh my god” everything is different type of change. Actually what we are doing
here is a very methodical, step by step, way to make your mind work differently. We are
opening up new neural pathways in how you look at things. We start with a new way to
look at our thoughts, emotions, behaviors and beliefs. Specifically you are training your
mind to not get wrapped up in emotional drama stories. We are training your mind to
actually adopt a perspective outside the emotional drama. We are training your mind to
not look at “what he did” or “what she said” but rather to be self aware, and self
reflective with your attention while these emotions and thoughts are happening. You
have to practice this multiple times for a certain number of hours until your mind does
this automatically.

It doesn’t really matter if you do it while at a computer typing, or hand writing, or with a
tape recorder. What is important is that practice making your mind operate in this
Observer Perspective until the neural pathways are opened up, and bigger than the old
ways. The key here is practice. That practice is a retraining of the mind so it begins to
see things from a different perspective. Once it does that, it will begin to make different
interpretations than it did in the past. These new interpretations will then create
different thoughts, which will have different emotions to them.

The actual work in opening up these new perspectives by practicing them through
writing, reading your writing, and listening to the recordings can not be over stated. If
you have ever seen the movie The Karate Kid you’ll understand the term “Wax on wax
off.”

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/Z4dkuYro4t8

You can’t solve these emotional belief problems from the perspective they were created
from. You have to change the perspective first, and to do that takes a particular
practice. Situations come faster than we have a chance to think, so we have to practice
so that whey the do come up, our shift to the observer perspective is automatic. If we
had t think to drive, hit a baseball, play an instrument, or even walk, our thinking would
be too slow and we wouldn’t be able to do it. We would fall down if we had to think
about all the things we had to move and adjust for. The reason we are able to do it is
that we have practiced so that these things are automatic. The same kind of practice is
necessary so we don’t get tripped up into emotional reactions, and perspectives of
virtual selves in our stories.
